summary: Read two binary trees. Each tree contains from 0 to 2000 nodes, and every node value lies between -104 and 104. Overlay the trees by matching positions. When both positions contain a node, the result stores the sum of the two values. When only one side contains a node, keep that node and everything under it. Write the overlaid tree. If one tree is empty, the result is the other tree.
notes: The left column is this sample's input text and the right column is the text the program should print. Comparison ignores trailing newlines.
